windows.name: Windows
windows.description: Windows 10 and 11 client work: Group Policy, Windows Update, Defender, networking, and the settings an administrator actually changes.

windows-server.name: Windows Server
windows-server.description: Active Directory, DNS, DHCP, file and print services, Group Policy, and day-to-day care of Windows Server hosts.

linux.name: Linux
linux.description: Distributions, systemd, package management, filesystems and permissions on the machines that do not have a desktop.

macos.name: macOS
macos.description: Managing Macs in a mixed fleet: MDM enrolment, defaults, permissions, and the Unix-shaped parts underneath.

powershell.name: PowerShell
powershell.description: PowerShell 5.1 and 7 for real administration: remoting, CIM, pipelines, error handling and scripts that are safe to run twice.

bash.name: Bash and Shell
bash.description: Shell scripting for systems work: quoting done right, exit codes, `set -euo pipefail`, and small scripts that survive contact with production.

networking.name: Networking
networking.description: DNS, DHCP, routing, VLANs, firewalls and the layered packet walk that turns "it won't connect" into a specific hop.

active-directory.name: Active Directory
active-directory.description: Domains, OU design, group policy, replication, Kerberos and the identity plumbing an organisation runs on.

security.name: Security
security.description: Patching, hardening, least privilege, key and certificate handling, and first-response triage when something looks wrong.

helpdesk.name: Help Desk
helpdesk.description: Tier-1 workflows: remote support, ticket triage, repeatable diagnostics, and deflecting the same three tickets every week.

automation.name: Automation
automation.description: Task Scheduler, cron, configuration management and idempotent scripting — making the second run free.

virtualization.name: Virtualization
virtualization.description: Hyper-V, Proxmox, VMware ESXi, snapshots, checkpoints, and the backup conversations people postpone.

containers.name: Containers
containers.description: Docker and OCI images: building lean images, running with the right limits, and reading the logs when a container will not start.

kubernetes.name: Kubernetes
kubernetes.description: Clusters, deployments, services and manifests for administrators who did not write the platform.

ci-cd.name: CI/CD
ci-cd.description: Pipelines, GitHub Actions, build and release automation, and keeping a pipeline honest as it grows.

cloud.name: Cloud
cloud.description: AWS, Azure and Google Cloud day-to-day operations: IAM, quotas, storage classes, billing and cost surprises.

cloudflare.name: Cloudflare
cloudflare.description: DNS, Workers, Pages, R2, WAF and Zero Trust for the team that owns the zone rather than the vendor contract.

backup-recovery.name: Backup and Recovery
backup-recovery.description: Designing backups you have actually restored, retention that does not fill the disk, and rehearsing a recovery.

storage.name: Storage
storage.description: Disks, RAID, SMART, filesystems, quotas, shares and the space emergency at 02:00.

monitoring.name: Monitoring
monitoring.description: Metrics, logs, uptime checks and alerting — including how to build an alert somebody will actually read.

dns.name: DNS
dns.description: Zone design, record types, and the "why can't I resolve this" chase: dig, nslookup, zone transfers, and split-brain resolvers.

azure.name: Microsoft Azure
azure.description: The Azure surfaces IT actually manages: identities and access, storage, virtual machines, diagnostics, and the billing rules that surprise people.

aws.name: Amazon Web Services
aws.description: The AWS surfaces IT actually manages: IAM, S3, EC2, VPC, CloudWatch, and the cost centres that quietly grow.

databases.name: Databases
databases.description: Data-model fundamentals, indexes, locking, and the daily admin of keeping a production database fast, backed up and upgradable.

sql-server.name: SQL Server
sql-server.description: Always On, maintenance plans, backups, and the service-pack-and-cumulative-update treadmill on the servers that hold the company's data.

postgresql.name: PostgreSQL
postgresql.description: psql and pgAdmin day-to-day: vacuum, replication, logical decoding, and extending a Postgres install without breaking the people who depend on it.
